newsitem.title: HONG KONG: British Airways adds flights for HK '97.
newsitem.headline: British Airways adds flights for HK '97.

text.p: British Airways Plc said on Friday it would run three extra flights between Hong Kong and London to accommodate an increase in passenger demand during the territory's changeover to Chinese rule on July 1.
The carrier, which now operates twice daily services between London and Hong Kong, will add two extra services, both departing from London on June 28.
It will also operate an additional flight departing Hong Kong on July 2, it said in a statement.
Hong Kong, a British colony of over 150 years, reverts to Chinese rule at midnight June 30.
Hong Kong people working overseas and tourists wishing to see the historic event have reserved flights back to the territory, many of them months ahead of the handover.
